key_patterns: Every script is heavily commented with a WHY-shaped XML doc block and prose comments that argue the design decision; match that voice or the diff will look foreign. Tunable numbers normally live on the VehicleTuning ScriptableObject and are read live every frame - but that asset is FROZEN for this task, so every new knob here is a [Tooltip] + [SerializeField] private field on the MonoBehaviour itself (ChaseCamera, VehicleJumpFlip, PlaytestLogger). Scene files carry no entry for a field that did not exist when they were saved, so Unity falls back to the C# initialiser and no scene edit is needed. Camera easing uses SmoothingFactor(smoothTime, dt) = 1 - exp(-dt/smoothTime) for frame-rate independence; ChaseCamera.SnapToTarget must reset any new camera state because VehicleMeasurement.ResetCar calls it before every reading (VehicleMeasurement.cs:1016-1017). VehicleJumpFlip buffers input (inputBufferTime 0.12) and gates moves behind cooldowns with a Refuse(reason) debug line per gate. PlaytestLogger accumulates seconds in FixedUpdate next to _handbrakeSeconds and reads counters as 'now minus value at shift start' (see _flipsAtStart).
